desc:
You are given an array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, in which every value is smaller than 2bits. You run n = nums.length rounds. In each round:

  1. Choose an integer k with 0 ≤ k < 2bits that maximises the XOR of k with all elements currently in the array, and record k.
  2. Remove the last element of the array.

Return the list of recorded values k, one per round, in order.

nums = [0, 1, 1, 3], bits = 2
round 1: XOR of all = 0^1^1^3 = 3, best k = 0  (3^0 = 3)
round 2: [0, 1, 1] XOR = 0, best k = 3
round 3: [0, 1] XOR = 1, best k = 2
round 4: [0] XOR = 0, best k = 3
result = [0, 3, 2, 3]
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: Let X be the XOR of the current elements. You want to choose k so that X ^ k is as large as possible. What is the largest value below 2bits?
The best X ^ k is all ones in the lowest bits positions, i.e. 2bits - 1. That forces k to be the bitwise complement of X inside those bits.
Compute the XOR of the whole array once, then for each round output X ^ (2bits - 1) and XOR away the removed last element to update X.
editorial: For a fixed XOR value X < 2bits, the maximum of X ^ k over k < 2bits is the all-ones mask M = 2bits - 1, reached exactly when k = X ^ M. That choice of k is unique, so the answer is deterministic.

The elements removed are always the last ones, so the XOR needed in round i is a prefix XOR of the array: the XOR of the first n - i elements. Compute the prefix XORs in one pass (or the total XOR and peel off elements from the end by XOR-ing them again) and map each to its complement. O(n) time, O(1) extra space besides the output.
